Who We Are

Our Story

"We didn't set out to build a restaurant. We set out to feed our community."

Est. 2020 · Oye-Ekiti

Where It Began

From a Family Kitchen to Oye-Ekiti's Table

De Labubu's Taste began with a simple belief: that good food is one of the most powerful forms of love. What started as cooking for family gatherings quickly grew into something larger — a community gathering point where people from all walks of life could share a table.

We opened our doors in 2020 with a small menu, big hearts, and an unshakeable commitment to quality. No cutting corners. No compromise on ingredients. Every pot stirred with intention, every plate sent out with pride.

Today, De Labubu's Taste serves hundreds of customers weekly — families, students, professionals and visitors. The food has evolved. The menu has grown. But the heart of what we do has never changed.

What Drives Us

Our Core Values

01

Freshness, Always

We shop the market every morning. If it's not fresh, it doesn't leave our kitchen.

02

Community First

We are part of Oye-Ekiti. We hire locally, source locally, and give back locally.

03

Respect on Every Plate

Every customer gets the same quality and care — whether ordering a ₦500 snack or a full corporate spread.

04

Cultural Pride

Egusi, jollof, pepper soup, ofada — these are not just dishes. They are identity, memory, and heritage.

Our Mission

"To nourish the people of Oye-Ekiti and beyond with food that is honest, soulful, and made with genuine care — so that every customer feels truly at home."

— The De Labubu's Taste Team
